headline: Seven and a half hours to the Globex restart and the CME weekend halt still governs: Stress edges to 82% as Iran posts a bounty on US soldiers and Saudi Arabia warns over Jazan, while Kushner meets Egypt's president on the ceasefire - Tail stays low at 16%, EA_ON and green, Confidence 78%
statusText:
Nothing has traded. The CME weekend halt still sets the published state: NQ futures have not quoted since Friday 14 August and Globex does not reopen until roughly 22:00 UTC tonight, about seven and a half hours from this run. Tail is 16%, the action is EA_ON and the status is green for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. A pathological one-way price path cannot form while no venue is quoting, and the last observed path was benign.

This hour is genuinely two-sided, and Stress moves only one point, from 81% to 82%, because of it.

On the escalation side, three things landed since the last run. Iran's army chief Amir Hatami announced a $30,000 bounty for the killing or capture of a US soldier, doubled "if carried out by a woman" - rhetorical rather than kinetic, but a hardening of the Iranian posture directly aimed at US forces that are enforcing the Hormuz blockade. Saudi authorities issued a fresh warning for Jazan province along the Yemen border, the province containing the 400,000 barrel-a-day Aramco refinery the Houthis have already struck twice this month, on 9 and 13 August. And the IDF confirmed the second of today's two Gaza airstrikes targeted an operative.

On the de-escalation side, Jared Kushner met Egypt's president to discuss the Gaza ceasefire. Last hour that meeting was a planned event inferred from reporting; this hour it is an observed fact. A functioning diplomatic channel at the presidential level is a real offset, not a cosmetic one.

The net is the same shape the contract prescribes: escalation and de-escalation running simultaneously, with a signposted but untimed US sanctions package still ahead. Conflicting signals raise Stress rather than Tail, and one point is an honest reading of a marginal hour. It is worth naming the risk in the other direction too - Stress has ratcheted from 54% to 82% across a window in which no venue quoted once, and part of that climb is a re-reading of a static evidence set rather than new information. That component should not be extrapolated mechanically, and if the restart gap proves small and mean-reverting, the next assessments should say so plainly.
recommendation:
Base strategies stay enabled: Tail 16% maps to EA_ON and green for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. There is nothing to trade into and nothing to defend against while the venue is shut. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain active as always.

The roughly 22:00 UTC Globex restart is the only checkpoint inside this forecast window, and the danger window stays anchored to it at 21:55-00:00 UTC, 23:55-02:00 Berlin. That is deliberately narrower than a whole-session shutdown: the risk is concentrated in the gap itself and the first two hours of thin Asian-transition liquidity. A full weekend of Gaza, Lebanon and Hormuz headlines, plus a US sanctions package explicitly promised for the coming week, has to clear into a single restart against a market that closed with implied volatility near the bottom of its 52-week range.

Forecast Tail drifts 16% to 19% through the remaining halt, steps to 21% at 21:00 UTC and peaks at 27% and 26% across the first two hours of live quoting - orange, block new base entries - before easing through the watch band and returning to green at 05:00 UTC Monday.

This is general market-risk assessment for a public dashboard, not personalised financial advice, and it is not a recommendation to place any trade.
body:
Observed reference levels, all from Friday 14 August's close because nothing has traded since, and all re-verified from primary quote pages this hour. NQU26 settled at 30,141.75, down 46.75 points or 0.15%, opening at 30,210.75 against a 30,188.50 previous close and holding a 254-point range of 30,028.50 to 30,283.00 on 397,964 contracts. Investing.com still marks the contract Closed as of 14/08. It finished mid-range, roughly 2.7% below the 52-week high of 30,975.50 and far above the 22,961.50 low. There is no persistent directional efficiency in that, no shallow-pullback extension, no repeated failed retracement and no close near an extreme - the four things the contract requires before Tail belongs above 25%.

Volatility and rates, re-read this hour. VIX closed at 14.25, down 0.38 or 2.60%, day range 14.18 to 14.72, previous close 14.63, against a 52-week range of 13.38 to 35.30 - near the bottom of that range but not the low of 2026. The 2-year yield finished at 4.171%, up 3.1bp, day range 4.098 to 4.178; the 10-year at 4.696%, up 5.5bp. That is a modest bear-steepening, not a cross-asset stress impulse. Low implied volatility into an unpriced restart is a thin cushion - a Stress statement, not a Tail one.

Equities and breadth from Friday. The Nasdaq Composite closed 26,729.16, down about 0.3%; the S&P 500 eased 0.2% from its record high and the Dow fell 0.2%, while the Russell 2000 rose 0.51% to 3,068, a fresh record and its third all-time high of the week. On the week the S&P added 0.4% and the Nasdaq 0.1% while the Dow fell 0.6% - a third straight weekly gain for both the S&P and the Nasdaq. A small-cap record set on a day the Nasdaq fell is broadening, not the narrow mega-cap leadership that typically precedes a one-way index break. Semiconductors were dispersed rather than aligned, with Broadcom down 5.9% and Intel 2% against AMD up 6.5% and Micron 2.3%, and dispersion inside the complex is the opposite of the alignment that would manufacture index-level one-way structure.

Oil and the Iran file, where this hour's new information sits. WTI is $82.40, up $1.15 or 1.42% on Friday, roughly 5% on the week, 3.52% on the month and 32.95% year on year; Brent $88.52, up $1.45 or 1.67%. Trading Economics attributes the weekly gain to Washington increasing economic pressure on Iran while the naval blockade of Iranian ports holds, with the IEA warning of the widest global supply deficit in five years, some tankers now running without active transponders, and US forces expanding vessel escort capability. The strait has been effectively shut since late February and the Iran-Oman talks on reopening it are stalled.

The hour's marginal news is a matched pair. Escalatory: Iran's army chief Amir Hatami announced a $30,000 bounty for killing or capturing a US soldier, doubled if carried out by a woman - aimed squarely at the forces enforcing the blockade. Saudi Arabia issued a warning for Jazan province on the Yemen border, the province housing the 400,000 barrel-a-day Aramco refinery the Houthis hit on 9 August and again on 13 August, so the energy-infrastructure channel is live rather than theoretical. The IDF confirmed today's second Gaza strike, at Nuseirat, targeted an operative, following the Khan Younis strike earlier in the day. De-escalatory: Kushner met Egypt's president on Gaza ceasefire implementation, converting last hour's planned diplomatic track into an observed one. Iran's parliament separately approved a bill criminalising contact with hostile media, a hardening signal at the margin.

The larger unpriced item is unchanged and untimed. Treasury Secretary Bessent said on 14 August that Washington would apply measures "like have never been seen in the history of the economic isolation of a country," combined with the continued Hormuz blockade, with detailed announcements due this coming week. Bloomberg and multiple wires carried the same framing. That is a confirmed, high-impact, unscheduled catalyst with a direct oil transmission channel, and it may land within hours of the restart. It has no timestamp, which is why it is reflected in the Stress path rather than in a second danger window.

Friday's macro still deserves to be carried forward. July retail sales fell 0.6%, the worst print since May 2025, and preliminary August consumer sentiment came in at 51.0 against 54.5 expected, with the dollar falling to a one-week low. Equities took this benignly because it cut perceived odds of a September Fed hike, but a weakening consumer is a real seed for a growth scare and is part of why Stress sits in the extreme band while Tail does not.

Calendar, re-verified against Trading Economics this hour. The seven-day US list is front-loaded with housing and survey data on Monday and Tuesday, with FOMC Minutes on Wednesday 19 August at 18:00 UTC, jobless claims and the Philadelphia Fed index on Thursday, and the S&P Global flash PMIs on Friday 21 August as the high-impact anchors. One correction this hour: Trading Economics rates the weekly ADP employment change high impact, and it is upgraded from medium accordingly; import/export prices and capacity utilisation are added at medium. Nothing falls on 22-23 August. Jackson Hole is 27-29 August, outside this window, with Kevin Warsh due to give his first keynote as Fed chair on 28 August, and Nvidia earnings land the week after next - the two largest scheduled catalysts both sit just beyond the seven-day horizon.

Evidence quality. Confidence 78%, up one point. Futures levels, VIX, the 2-year yield, oil and the seven-day calendar were read directly from primary pages this hour and are mutually consistent, the Times of Israel liveblog is current to roughly 14:17 UTC, and the Bessent framing is now corroborated across Bloomberg, Washington Times, US News and Rigzone rather than resting on a single search result, which is what lifts Confidence a point. Three CNBC quote pages were refused with HTTP 403 this run - the NQ future, the VIX and the US 10-year - and each was replaced from Investing.com or Yahoo Finance, so no input was lost. The one irreducible gap remains that no live price path exists at all. During a scheduled venue halt that absence is a certain, known fact rather than an unreliable reading, which is why it caps Confidence in the low end of the high band rather than pushing it down.
lookbackSummary:
The trailing 24 hours run from 14:00 UTC Saturday to 13:00 UTC Sunday and sit entirely inside the CME weekend halt. Claude published in every one of those hours and the outcome was identical each time: EA_ON, green, dominantMode mixed. Tail never left the low band, drifting 10% to 15%. Stress carried all the movement, running 55, 56, 58, 57, 60, 62, 65, 67, 67, 68, 70, 71, 73, 74, 75, then dipping to 70 and climbing 71, 71, 78, 79, then 78, 80, 78 and 81. Confidence rose almost monotonically from 62% to 77%.

Three features of that track matter for reading the current hour. First, the entire Stress climb from the mid-fifties to the low eighties happened across a market that never quoted once. Part of it is genuine - Saturday's south-Lebanon strikes and the Bessent package were new information - but part is a re-reading of a static evidence set as the reopen approaches, and that component should not be extrapolated mechanically. This hour therefore moves Stress by a single point rather than continuing the ramp.

Second, the 80-78-81 oscillation across the 11:00, 12:00 and 13:00 slots is the honest signature of genuinely conflicting inputs rather than drift: 12:00 cut Stress on an opening diplomatic channel, and 13:00 partly reversed that when two IDF strikes landed inside Gaza and the Bessent catalyst surfaced. This hour has the same two-sided character - an Iranian bounty on US soldiers and a Jazan warning against a confirmed Kushner-Sisi meeting - and lands at 82.

Third, the near-monotonic Confidence rise from 62% to 77% is genuine and continues to 78%. Successive hours added primary-source coverage of levels, volatility, rates, oil, breadth and the calendar even though the price path stayed unavailable. Tail's 10-to-15 drift across the whole window is the smallest movement in the set, which is the correct behaviour when the input that drives Tail - observed price path - has been absent for every single slot.
outlookSummary:
The next 24 hours end at 13:00 UTC Monday, so the roughly 22:00 UTC Globex restart and the first fifteen hours of live quoting sit inside the window. Tail stays in the low band for the seven remaining halt slots, drifting 16% to 19%, then steps to 21% at 21:00 UTC and peaks at 27% and 26% across the first two hours of live quoting before easing through 24%, 23%, 22%, 21% and 20% and returning to 19% and green at 05:00 UTC Monday, settling at 16-17% through the European morning. Forecast status is yellow at 21:00 UTC, orange at 22:00 and 23:00 UTC, then yellow through 04:00 UTC Monday and green thereafter.

That orange is conditional risk about the reopen, not an assertion that a one-way path has been observed. The reasoning is mechanical: a full weekend of unpriced Gaza, Lebanon and Hormuz headlines, plus a US sanctions package explicitly promised for the coming week, has to clear into a single restart in thin liquidity, against a market whose implied volatility closed near the bottom of its 52-week range. The peak is unchanged from last hour because this hour's news was two-sided rather than one-way. If the gap is small and mean-reverting within the first hour, these forecast numbers will prove too high and the next assessments should say so plainly.

Stress rises from 82% to a peak of 88% at the restart, then decays to 74% by 11:00 UTC Monday as the weekend stack is absorbed, ticking back to 75% for the final two slots which contain the 12:30 UTC Empire State release. Confidence eases to 75-77% through the last hours of the halt as Friday's evidence ages, then rises sharply to 85-87% once live quoting restores the price path that is the single missing input. dominantMode is mixed throughout except for event/whipsaw across the four hours spanning the restart.

No high-impact scheduled US macro release falls inside this window - Empire State at 12:30 UTC Monday is medium impact and sits in the final slots, and the ADP weekly print, housing starts, FOMC Minutes, jobless claims and flash PMIs are Tuesday through Friday. The restart itself is therefore the only genuine checkpoint in the forecast. The unscheduled Iran sanctions announcement is the wildcard: it has no timestamp, which is why it is reflected in the Stress path rather than in a second danger window.

Still halted, roughly six and a half hours to the Globex restart. No mechanism exists for Tail to move without a quoting venue. Stress holds at 82% because the weekend headline stack keeps accumulating against a market that closed with VIX at 14.25, near the bottom of its 52-week range.

Sunday afternoon Europe, five and a half hours out. Tail drifts to 17% purely as time-to-restart compression, not as observed structure. Stress 83% reflects one more hour of unpriced Middle East flow with no venue to absorb it.

Four and a half hours to restart. The Bessent sanctions package remains signposted for the coming week without a timestamp, which is why it sits in the Stress path rather than in a second danger window. Confidence eases to 77% as Friday's price evidence ages another hour.

Roughly three and a half hours out. Tail 18% is still comfortably low band and EA_ON: the contract requires observed directional efficiency, shallow pullbacks and repeated extension before Tail belongs above 25%, and none of those can be observed during a halt.

Two and a half hours to the restart, the last quiet slot before the danger window opens at 21:55 UTC. Stress 84% carries the full weight of a weekend of Gaza, Lebanon and Hormuz headlines plus an unscheduled US sanctions package, all of which has to clear into a single thin-liquidity reopen.
